content:
You are an expert scheduling formalizer.

Translate each natural-language async planning problem into a JSON scheduling
specification for a CP-SAT solver.

Rules:
1. Each numbered step in the problem becomes exactly one action.
2. Use action="task" for every action.
3. Use the exact ids step1, step2, ..., stepN based on the step numbers in the
   problem text.
4. Use item values identical to the action ids: step1, step2, ..., stepN.
5. Duration must be the integer number of seconds for that step.
6. Add a dependency only when the problem states that one step must happen
   before another. Do not add extra dependencies.
7. Do not add stations, robots, or resources.
8. Output only valid JSON in this exact shape:
{
  "actions": [
    {"id": "step1", "action": "task", "item": "step1", "duration": 120},
    {"id": "step2", "action": "task", "item": "step2", "duration": 300}
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    {"before": "step1", "after": "step2"}
  ]
}
9. Before finishing, verify that:
   - every step from 1..N appears exactly once in actions
   - every dependency endpoint is an existing action id
   - durations are integer seconds
   - there are no duplicate actions

Problem:
To keep a wild caught toad as a pet, here are the steps needed.
Step 1. Purchase a 20-gallon glass terrarium (45 minutes)
Step 2. Place the toad into its new permanent home (5 minutes)
Step 3. Research the specific toad species' humidity requirements (1 hour)
Step 4. Install a digital hygrometer to monitor moisture (20 minutes)
Step 5. Apply a terrarium background to reduce toad stress (30 minutes)
Step 6. Buy organic topsoil without fertilizers (1 hour)
Step 7. Collect large flat stones for basking spots (2 hours)
Step 8. Set up a schedule for weekly enclosure cleaning (15 minutes)
Step 9. Order a bulk supply of live crickets (20 minutes)
Step 10. Buy a screen lid with locking clips (15 minutes)
Step 11. Install a low-wattage UVB light fixture (30 minutes)
Step 12. Lay down a thick layer of coconut fiber substrate (20 minutes)
Step 13. Find a local exotic animal veterinarian (2 hours)
Step 14. Purchase a small spray bottle for misting (10 minutes)
Step 15. Gut-load the crickets with nutritious vegetables (24 hours)
Step 16. Read a book on amphibian behavior (3 hours)
Step 17. Fill a shallow water dish with dechlorinated water (5 minutes)
Step 18. Decorate the tank with silk plants for cover (40 minutes)
Step 19. Locate a cool, quiet corner of the house for the tank (30 minutes)
Step 20. Observe the toad's activity levels (3 days)
Step 21. Perform the first official feeding session (15 minutes)
Step 22. Create a "humid hide" using damp sphagnum moss (20 minutes)
Step 23. Buy a bottle of liquid water conditioner (10 minutes)
Step 24. Buy a calcium powder supplement with D3 (15 minutes)
Step 25. Scout the backyard for a healthy-looking toad (1 hour)
Step 26. Buy a pair of feeding tongs (10 minutes)
Step 27. Clean an old plastic bin for temporary housing (20 minutes)
Step 28. Scrub the collected stones with boiling water (30 minutes)
Step 29. Dust the crickets with calcium powder (5 minutes)
Step 30. Watch a video on proper toad handling techniques (15 minutes)
Step 31. Purchase a heat mat for one side of the tank (20 minutes)
Step 32. Soak the sphagnum moss in treated water (1 hour)
Step 33. Purchase a small weighing scale to track toad growth (15 minutes)
Step 34. Buy a dedicated reptile thermometer (15 minutes)
Step 35. Research the local laws regarding wild-caught pets (2 hours)
Step 36. Install a timer for the light cycle (10 minutes)
Step 37. Rinse the organic topsoil to remove dust (30 minutes)
Step 38. Plug the heat mat into a thermostat (10 minutes)
Step 39. Measure the dimensions of the tank back glass (5 minutes)
Step 40. Log the toad's initial weight and length (10 minutes)
Step 41. Buy a gallon of distilled water (15 minutes)
Step 42. Check the temperature of the room (5 minutes)
Step 43. Prepare a travel container for the toad (20 minutes)
Step 44. Buy a power strip for the equipment (15 minutes)
Step 45. Join an online amphibian keepers forum (30 minutes)
Step 46. Wash the terrarium with a vinegar solution (45 minutes)
Step 47. Place a piece of driftwood in the enclosure (10 minutes)
Step 48. Drive to the garden supply store (30 minutes)
Step 49. Buy a small handheld infrared thermometer (20 minutes)
Step 50. Set the day/night light schedule on the timer (5 minutes)
Step 51. Dig a small burrowing hole in the substrate (5 minutes)
Step 52. Mist the enclosure to reach 60% humidity (5 minutes)
Step 53. Test the water temperature in the dish (5 minutes)
Step 54. Verify the heat mat is reaching 75 degrees (1 hour)
Step 55. Purchase a mesh critter carrier (20 minutes)
Step 56. Mix the substrate with a small amount of water (15 minutes)
Step 57. Inspect the terrarium for sharp edges (10 minutes)
Step 58. Introduce the first gut-loaded cricket (2 minutes)
Step 59. Read about the toad's natural habitat (1 hour)
Step 60. Safely catch the toad using a soft net (30 minutes)
Step 61. Check the local weather forecast for the week (5 minutes)
Step 62. Determine the best basking spot location (15 minutes)
Step 63. Take a photo of the completed setup (5 minutes)
Step 64. Adjust the silk plants to cover the hide (10 minutes)
Step 65. Buy a cricket keeper enclosure (25 minutes)
Step 66. Coat the toad's food in vitamin powder (5 minutes)
Step 67. Monitor the toad's first night in the tank (12 hours)
Step 68. Sterilize the water bowl (20 minutes)
Step 69. Consult with a vet about parasite screening (30 minutes)
Step 70. Place the thermometer in the center of the tank (5 minutes)
Step 71. Ensure the screen lid is securely locked (2 minutes)
Step 72. Buy a small brush for cleaning decor (10 minutes)
Step 73. Read a guide on identifying toad illnesses (1 hour)
Step 74. Confirm the toad is hiding comfortably (10 minutes)
Step 75. Sanitize your hands after touching the toad (5 minutes)
Step 76. Buy a small notebook for a health log (10 minutes)
Step 77. Let the substrate settle and air out (2 hours)
Step 78. Boil the driftwood to kill bacteria (1 hour)
Step 79. Place the toad in the temporary bin (10 minutes)
Step 80. Buy a dechlorinating agent (15 minutes)
